brief_intent.critique: The screen substantively delivers the core brief: a stats sidebar (level 34, XP bar, 3 available skill points), a title (Skill Codex), and a connected-node skill tree as the centerpiece. However, several intent-level elements are weakened or ambiguous. (1) The skill tree reads as four disconnected vertical columns with only a single horizontal connector through the center node, so the 'matrix of connected nodes' feels under-realized—most nodes have no visible inter-branch relationships, undermining the 'tree' intent. (2) Node states are unclear: the legend lists Learned/Mastered/Locked, but nearly all nodes look identical (bright, active) with no visually distinct locked or mastered states, so the state system is not legible. (3) The 'available skill points' and the tree are not visually linked—there is no indication of which nodes are spendable/next, so the leveling interaction intent is weak. (4) The title 'Skill Codex' is small and tucked into a header bar rather than reading as a strong screen title, weakening hierarchy intent. (5) The loadout list is cut off at the bottom (third item clipped), suggesting the sidebar content is not fully contained.
brief_intent.suggestion: Prioritize these fixes: 1) Add more visible connecting paths between branches (e.g., cross-links, prerequisite lines, or a clear branching topology) so the centerpiece reads as a true connected skill tree/matrix, not four isolated columns. 2) Differentiate node states visually—dim/gray locked nodes, a distinct 'mastered' treatment, and a highlighted 'spendable/next' ring on nodes that can be unlocked with the 3 available points—so the legend and the leveling mechanic are legible. 3) Tie the 3 available skill points to the tree (e.g., pulse or badge on unlockable nodes, or a 'spend' affordance) to make the leveling intent explicit. 4) Promote the title to a stronger, larger screen heading so hierarchy matches the brief's emphasis. 5) Ensure the sidebar (loadout list) is fully visible without clipping, and confirm the XP bar and level are the dominant stats as intended.

clarity_hierarchy.critique: The primary focal point is ambiguous and the reading order is broken. The skill tree, which is the brief's centerpiece, is visually flattened: all nodes are nearly identical in size and luminance, so the eye has no entry point and no sense of which node is 'next' or most important. The only larger node (the central gold 'LV 3') is buried in the middle of the canvas rather than anchored, and its dashed 'active' ring is too subtle to read as a state. The sidebar competes for attention: the large '34' level number, the bright XP bar, and the glowing '3 available' skill-point card all pull focus away from the tree, creating three competing focal points. The four stat tiles (Power/Vitality/Focus/Resolve) are a dense, flat 2x2 grid with no hierarchy, and the Loadout list below is cramped and visually disconnected from the stats above it. The tree's four color-coded branches (Pyromancy, Runecraft, etc.) are not grouped or labeled in the canvas itself, so the relationship between the bottom legend and the columns is unclear. The 'LV 1' / 'LV 3' labels are tiny and low-contrast, making node states hard to parse at a glance. The top-right header pills ('3 points to spend', '18 of 28 skills') duplicate sidebar information, adding noise without clarifying hierarchy.
clarity_hierarchy.suggestion: 1) Establish a single dominant focal point: make the skill tree the clear hero by increasing the canvas contrast and giving the 'active/next' node a much stronger visual treatment (larger scale, brighter glow, or a pulsing ring) so the eye lands there first. 2) Create a clear reading order in the sidebar: top-to-bottom as Identity → Level/XP → Skill Points (make this the primary call-to-action with the strongest accent) → Stats → Loadout. Reduce the visual weight of the '34' level number and the XP bar so they support, not compete with, the skill-point action. 3) Group the four stat tiles into a single labeled 'Attributes' block with a subtle container to reduce visual fragmentation, and separate the Loadout list with a clear section header and more breathing room. 4) Add in-canvas branch labels (e.g., small headers above each column: 'Pyromancy', 'Runecraft', etc.) to connect the legend to the tree and clarify grouping. 5) Increase the size and contrast of node level labels and state indicators (Learned/Mastered/Locked) so node status is readable without hovering. 6) Remove or de-emphasize the duplicate top-right pills to reduce competing information and keep the header focused on the title.

visual_system_craft.critique: The skill tree's central hub node (Lv 3) is visually inconsistent with the rest of the system: it is significantly larger, uses a different ring treatment (dashed halo), and its icon is a generic diamond rather than a branch-specific glyph, breaking the node grammar. The connecting lines are a single flat gold color regardless of branch, which contradicts the color-coded branch system (Pyromancy=orange, Runecraft=blue, etc.) and makes the tree read as a single undifferentiated mesh rather than four distinct paths. The 'Lv 1' / 'Lv 3' labels beneath nodes are extremely low-contrast and inconsistent in placement—some are centered, some appear offset—and the font size is so small it is nearly illegible. The sidebar's stat cards (Power, Vitality, Focus, Resolve) use a 2x2 grid with inconsistent internal padding: the top row cards have more vertical breathing room than the bottom row. The XP bar's fill color (gold) does not semantically map to any branch or state, and its track has no visible border or inset, making it look flat against the dark background. The 'Loadout' section's skill entries use a dashed separator that is too faint and inconsistent in weight with the solid borders used elsewhere. The bottom legend bar's 'States' section uses a dashed line for 'Active' that is nearly invisible against the dark background, and the 'Locked' state has no visual indicator at all. The overall spacing rhythm between the sidebar sections is uneven—the gap between the XP bar and Skill Points card is larger than the gap between Skill Points and the stat grid.
visual_system_craft.suggestion: 1. Unify node geometry: make all nodes the same diameter (or use a consistent 1.2x scale for hub nodes only) and apply the same ring stroke treatment across all. Replace the generic diamond icon on the hub with a branch-specific glyph or a composite icon. 2. Color-code the connecting lines to match their branch (orange for Pyromancy, blue for Runecraft, etc.) and use a consistent stroke width. 3. Increase the contrast and size of the 'Lv' labels beneath nodes, and ensure they are consistently centered. 4. Standardize the internal padding of the stat cards in the sidebar to create a uniform 2x2 grid. 5. Add a subtle inset or border to the XP bar track to give it depth, and consider using a gradient or a color that maps to the player's primary branch. 6. Increase the opacity of the dashed separators in the Loadout section and ensure they match the weight of other borders. 7. Make the 'Active' state indicator in the legend more visible (e.g., use a brighter dashed line or a different symbol) and add a visual indicator for the 'Locked' state (e.g., a grayed-out circle or a lock icon). 8. Tighten the vertical spacing rhythm in the sidebar to create a consistent gap between all sections.
